rule: approved design. Version-13 value code 30 gains a second shape, `(30, [Type(signature), Value(callee), Range(arguments), Flag(safety)])`, read as `ValueKind::PointerCall` and admitted only under the body-node profile; a direct call keeps `(30, [Type, Value, Range])` and the read matches the whole operand slice. The flag is the request codec's: 0 Safe, 1 ExplicitUnsafeBlock, 2 UnsafeFunction. A pointer call owns no request row: its site is its one evaluation. Every consumer re-proves the signature against the callee's closed Rust pointer type node by node (convention, variadicness, unsafety, arity, parameters and result) and the safety with direct Call's own matrix, at validation and again over the rebuilt body; local lowering calls the pointer value. Q3 Branch A also admits constructor reification: each consumer defines its own constructor instance. Existing packets keep their bytes: export fenced both forms before

cases.shape: `unsafe { base::bare_call(base::raw) }`: an unsafe fn calls its unsafe pointer parameter bare under `#[allow(unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn)]`
`base::block_call(base::raw)`: a safe fn calls its `unsafe fn(u8) -> i32` parameter in an unsafe block
`base::call_ptr(base::hold)`: a provider body calls its `fn(u8) -> i32` parameter; the client reifies its argument
`base::ctor()(41)` matched on its field: the tuple-struct constructor `P` reified to `fn(u8) -> P`; the consumer defines the constructor instance itself
`unsafe { base::fmt(20, 22, base::render) }`: the fmt-shaped twin, a free unsafe fn calling its `unsafe fn(u8, u8) -> i32` formatter parameter in an unsafe block
`base::apply_ptr(base::id::<u8>, 42u8) as i32`: `apply_ptr<T>` calls its `fn(T) -> T` parameter; the consumer instantiates it at u8
`base::Runner::run(base::hold)`: a safe pointer call in an inherent associated fn of a unit struct
`unsafe { base::nested_call(base::raw) }`: an unsafe fn calls its unsafe pointer parameter in an unsafe block
`base::reified_call()`: one provider body reifies `hold` to a local pointer and calls it
`base::safe_block(base::hold)`: a safe pointer called inside an unnecessary unsafe block records Safe, as a direct call does; rustc warns unused_unsafe on the provider
`base::some::<u8>()(41)` matched: the generic variant constructor `Opt::Some` reified to `fn(T) -> Opt<T>`; the consumer instantiates and defines it
`base::twice(inc, 40) as i32` with a client-local `inc`: two nested calls through one pointer
`base::variant()(41)` matched: the variant constructor `E::A` reified to `fn(u8) -> E`
